This page is the map. Full detail (module lists, prerequisites, the session-by-session plan)
lives in the repo at `plans/curriculum.md` — this is the reader-friendly version.

## The idea

A Director of IT Service Operations & Excellence at a multi-state blood services organization
needs to be credible in four directions at once: with FDA, with AABB, with the CIO, and with
the Quality Analyst who reports to him. That takes more than one course. It takes enough of the
blood-banking, regulatory, quality-systems, and risk-management world to ask the right question
and catch a wrong answer — without trying to become the Quality Analyst's job.

## Where the depth comes from

Several tracks below borrow their structure — not exam prep, structure — from professional
bodies of knowledge that have already solved "what does a competent person in this space need
to know" for an adjacent role:

- **NIST's Risk Management Framework** (the backbone of ISC2's CGRC certification) shapes the
  GRC track: categorize, select, implement, assess, authorize, monitor.
- **ISC2's HCISPP** body of knowledge (healthcare-specific security and privacy) shapes the
  healthcare security & privacy course.
- **SOC 2** (AICPA Trust Services Criteria) and **ISO/IEC 27001** shape the vendor and
  third-party risk course — reading vendor audit reports for what they actually cover.
- **ISO 13485 / FDA's Quality Management System Regulation** shapes how BECS gets framed:
  device-grade software, not ordinary enterprise IT.
- **ICH Q9 quality risk management** and **ASQ's Certified Quality Auditor** body of knowledge
  shape the deeper audit and risk content inside the quality-systems track.
- **AABB Quality System Essentials** remains the spine everything else has to map onto, since
  that's the accreditation the organization actually answers to.

## Seven things this curriculum builds

1. **How a blood center actually works** — donor to hospital, and where IT sits in that
   pipeline.
2. **How to read the regulatory landscape** — and speak one consistent risk vocabulary
   (likelihood, severity, inherent vs. residual risk) across every framework below.
3. **Quality systems** — deviations, CAPA, change control, document control, and a real
   internal audit program: the AABB Quality System Essentials, in practice.
4. **Validation, BECS, and device-grade quality systems** — reading a validation package, Part
   11 (including its messier hybrid-system and legacy-system corners), ALCOA+ data integrity,
   and where ISO 13485/QMSR fits.
5. **Governance, risk, and compliance** — running a system or vendor through a full
   categorize-to-monitor risk cycle, the same motion whether the framework is NIST RMF, ISO
   31000, or a validation release decision.
6. **Healthcare security, privacy, and vendor oversight** — HIPAA next to Part 11, reading a
   SOC 2 report and an ISO 27001 certificate, and handling a breach that triggers two
   regulators at once.
7. **The ITSM bridge and directing the Quality Analyst** — translating ITIL practice into
   AABB/NIST/ISO language for the CIO, and reviewing a direct report's work well enough to catch
   what an inspector would catch.

## Tracks

| Track | Courses |
|---|---|
| Foundations | Reading a CFR citation · The regulatory landscape · Risk & controls vocabulary |
| 1. Blood Center Operations | Blood center operations, donor to hospital |
| 2. Quality Systems & Compliance | Quality system essentials · FDA & AABB in practice (incl. internal audit program design) |
| 3. Validation, BECS & Data Integrity | CSV & BECS (incl. ISO 13485/QMSR) · Data integrity & records (incl. Part 11 predicate rules) |
| 4. Governance, Risk & Compliance | GRC frameworks & risk management · Healthcare security & privacy · Vendor & third-party risk (SOC 2, ISO 27001) |
| 5. ITSM Bridge | ITSM for regulated blood services *(capstone)* |
| 6. Directing the Quality Analyst | Directing the Quality Analyst |

## Recommended order

**First six months** — the day-to-day job: understand the business, run the quality systems,
and direct the Quality Analyst.

1. Foundations (regulatory landscape, risk vocabulary)
2. Blood center operations
3. Quality system essentials
4. Directing the Quality Analyst
5. CSV & BECS
6. Data integrity & records
7. FDA & AABB in practice (audit program design, inspection readiness)

**Months seven through roughly fourteen** — the deeper governance, security, and vendor layer,
finishing with the capstone.

8. GRC frameworks & risk management
9. Healthcare security & privacy
10. Vendor & third-party risk management
11. ITSM for regulated blood services *(capstone)*

## How courses appear here

Courses show up in the sidebar under **Courses** as they're built — one module at a time, one
module per work session. Nothing here is built yet; this page describes the plan.
